name.full: Mahir Vey of the Glass Mouth

epithet: who knelt in places no one else could find
mannerisms: looks past your shoulder when they answer
never sits with their back to a door
unclasps and reclasps belts when thinking
voice: precise as cut glass and just as hard to argue with
aspiration: to be left alone long enough to finish what they started
wound: a parent who left and called it work
secret: that the experience they claim to have had keeps slipping away

threads.desc: who has been chasing the same prize for so long that the chase is the friendship
(not theirs) who calls when nobody else does
who left without an argument, and whose silence {name} still rehearses answers to

backstory.origin: Born in The Forge, of the Glass Mouth, Mahir grew up in a household where one book was on every shelf and another had been forbidden.
backstory.weight: The family is built on a series of leavings. Two generations back, a father vanished into work and never quite returned. Mahir's parent learned to expect this kind of departure, and so did Mahir.
backstory.fracture: Somewhere in their fifteens, the floor gave way. What they touched on the other side has not left them, and they have, since then, been more interested in what is under things than what is on them.
backstory.between: Between then and now, they did most of the ordinary things. They lived in a house borrowed and not returned for a time, learned the names of the local birds, and grew briefly close to a person whose name they will not say in mixed company.
backstory.present: These days, Mahir can be found at the watch wall most mornings. They have a small icon they did not buy that they will not throw away, and a habit of speaking briefly aloud to the dead that even their oldest friends find slightly strange.
